title: Silvermoon City
body: Silvermoon has been the seat of the elves of Quel'Thalas since Dath'Remar Sunstrider and his exiled Highborne founded it and kindled the Sunwell, thousands of years ago. In the Third War the Scourge, led past the kingdom's defenses by the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir, sacked the city and set it ablaze. The Dead Scar, the road of ash the undead carved, still runs through it, and the western half lies in ruins. The eastern half has been raised again by the magisters under Grand Magister Rommath, its spires shining with arcane power. Here the blood elves keep their markets in the Bazaar and the Royal Exchange, their rogues and warlocks along Murder Row, and the Blood Knights in Farstriders' Square. From Sunfury Spire, Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron rules beside Rommath and Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing, and the city has long looked to Prince Kael'thas, far away in Outland.

title: The Shepherd's Gate
body: The Shepherd's Gate is the main road into Silvermoon from Eversong Woods. It is not the city's first entrance: the old gate was lost when the Scourge broke into Quel'Thalas, and its remains lie off along the Dead Scar. The new gate was named in honor of Prince Kael'thas, who passed through it into his ruined capital after the invasion, and a towering statue of the prince overlooks the approach. Just outside the walls Skymistress Gloaming keeps the dragonhawks that fly travelers and supplies south to Tranquillien, and just inside, on the Walk of Elders, a gatewatcher in Blood Knight colors has been seen bullying a frightened citizen.

title: Lor'themar Theron
body: Lor'themar Theron rose through the Farstriders to become ranger lord and second-in-command to Sylvanas Windrunner. When the Scourge overran Quel'Thalas and Sylvanas fell, he led the survivors, and Prince Kael'thas later named him Regent Lord, charged with guarding the land and seeking a cure for his people while the prince was away. Needing allies, he accepted the Forsaken's offer of aid, and he means to see the blood elves take their place in the Horde as equals. He holds court in Sunfury Spire with Grand Magister Rommath and Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing at his side.

parts.body: The death of the traitor Dar'Khan gave the regent the proof he needed. His letter went to Lady Sylvanas, who added her own seal, and on to Thrall in Orgrimmar, and the Warchief accepted the pledge of the sin'dorei: in the end, he admitted, the Horde needs them as much as they need the Horde.

parts.body: Then came a harder blow. Kael'thas has betrayed his people, and the regent bids them be strong and not lose heart. Arthas did not break their spirit when he swept through their land, he tells them, and neither will the prince: let it be a lesson to them all as they move toward a better future.

parts.body: In time Lor'themar stood within the restored Sunwell itself, beside Rommath, when Thalorien Dawnseeker's lost sword Quel'Delar was carried there to be cleansed. He had not thought he would live to see the blade made whole again, and he named its bearer a symbol of his people's endurance in the face of tragedy and treachery.

title: Grand Magister Rommath
body: Grand Magister Rommath leads the magisters of Quel'Thalas. He served with Kael'thas in the Alliance resistance in Lordaeron and was condemned to death with the prince's elves in the dungeons of Dalaran, a betrayal he has never forgiven the Kirin Tor. Sent home from Outland with a message of hope, he taught his people to draw arcane energy from crystals and other sources to ease their hunger for magic, and led the magisters who raised Silvermoon's spires anew. He also conceived the Blood Knights and chose Liadrin as the first. He stands at Lor'themar's side in Sunfury Spire.

title: Halduron Brightwing
body: Halduron Brightwing commands the Farstriders as Ranger-General, the post Sylvanas Windrunner held before the Scourge came. A veteran of the wars against the Amani, he once captured the troll Zul'jin, who escaped by hacking off his own arm. During the invasion of Quel'Thalas he saved his old friend Lor'themar from the undead, and when Lor'themar became regent, Halduron took up the leadership of the rangers. He has stood for his people's place in the Horde, and he has never approved of the Blood Knights.

title: Lady Liadrin
body: Orphaned by Amani trolls and raised in the faith by High Priest Vandellor, Liadrin became a high priestess of Quel'Thalas, then lost her faith when the Scourge laid her homeland waste. Grand Magister Rommath offered her a new path, and she became the first Blood Knight and matriarch of the order, whose knights claim a mastery of the Light that other paladins despise. The order keeps its headquarters in the Hall of Blood in Farstriders' Square, and her right hand there, Lord Solanar Bloodwrath, is a hero of the order in his own right.

title: Knight-Lord Bloodvalor
body: Knight-Lord Bloodvalor manages the rank-and-file of the Blood Knights from the Hall of Blood in Farstriders' Square, and it is he who sets the trials every initiate must pass. He has no patience for pleasantries, which he leaves to courtiers and their kind, and he keeps a close eye on any initiate whose progress is rapid. He welcomes visitors to the headquarters of the defenders of Quel'Thalas, the faithful servants of Silvermoon, and the true masters of the Light, and he charges his adepts to show neither mercy nor weakness and to defend their people and their brothers tirelessly.

parts.body: He believes a knight must be ready at every moment. It was Bloodvalor who sent Sangrias Stillblade to strike at an initiate kneeling in the First Trial, and he does not apologize for it: the order is a brotherhood, its brothers must be alert at all times, and if making the point costs a knight his life, that too is part of the training.

parts.body: Nor was Stillblade's service over. Bloodvalor had the fallen knight's body carried back to the city and laid in an upper room of the inn, so that the very initiate who killed him could restore him to life.

title: Magister Astalor Bloodsworn
body: Magister Astalor Bloodsworn, once among Prince Kael'thas's closest advisors, helped found the Blood Knights with the support of Grand Magister Rommath. He keeps to a hidden chamber beneath the Hall of Blood in Farstriders' Square, with magisters of his own about him, and it is to him that Knight-Lord Bloodvalor sends initiates once the First Trial is behind them, for their schooling in the order's ways has only begun. There he teaches them the nature and breadth of the order's power.

parts.body: The chamber holds the order's secret. Its Light was taken from a naaru that Kael'thas sent to Silvermoon as a gift, a being that begrudged the elves its power until Astalor's magisters devised a way to claim it on their own terms, and he helped Liadrin, the order's first knight, to reach it.

parts.body: He has nothing good to say of his old master now. He curses Kael'thas and his felbloods, who have taken all the order worked for, yet he insists the Blood Knights will fight back and will not be destroyed so easily, for Lady Liadrin already seeks a new source of power.

parts.body: It was the naaru that the felbloods took. The magisters who tended it were left dazed and drained, though faint vestiges of its Light still cling to them. Astalor has seen to their care, and he hands initiates an enchanted vessel to draw out what remains, just enough to restore a fallen comrade to life.

title: Lord Solanar Bloodwrath
body: Lord Solanar Bloodwrath is Lady Liadrin's right hand, one of the first sin'dorei to take up the Blood Knights' path and a hero in his own right. In the Hall of Blood he leaves the training of the rank-and-file to Knight-Lord Bloodvalor while he takes a personal hand in choosing the order's masters, an inner circle of its most dedicated and trusted knights, known to most only by their thalassian chargers. Solanar holds that the Blood Knights wield the Light as other so-called paladins never could, and that those false paladins should be shown their time has come to an end.

title: The Trials of the Blood Knights
body: Initiates who excel in their early training are summoned to Farstriders' Square by Knight-Lord Bloodvalor, who has no use for pleasantries and sets the trials that make a Blood Knight. Mastery of the Light, he teaches, demands a focused mind and great willpower, without which a knight is little better than a street thug. The First Trial tests exactly that. On the Isle of Tribulations in the northeastern Ghostlands, the initiate enters a shallow cave, kneels before a brazier, lights it and focuses on the visions it brings. Many set out on this path, and few last long enough to be called adept.

Earlier: Isle of Tribulations placed in the northeastern Ghostlands per quest 9678; adept rank order fixed (rank is granted after the materials, quest 9707).

parts.body: The visions were not the whole test. Sangrias Stillblade fell upon the kneeling initiate, sent by Bloodvalor himself to see whether a brother of the order stays alert at every moment, and Stillblade died for it. Even that, the knight-lord says, is as much a part of the training as any sword drill.
sources: quest 9678 reward text

parts.body: The Second Trial hides nothing. In a pavilion north of the city, beyond the Ruins of Silvermoon, Master Kelerun Bloodmourn sets four Blood Knight champions against the candidate, and those who best all four have proven themselves worthy of full membership, though a few tasks still stand between them and their new rank.
sources: quests 9690, 9686 descriptions and reward text

parts.body: The last duties were ceremonial but no less dangerous: gathering the materials for the order's blood-tempered ranseur and claiming a Blood Knight insignia, for each new adept inherits one from a veteran, this one from a knight who fell leading an assault on Deatholme. Then came the rank of adept, and the smith Bemarrin forged the weapon to match it.

title: The Captive Naaru
body: After the First Trial, Knight-Lord Bloodvalor sends initiates below the Hall of Blood to Magister Astalor Bloodsworn. Sangrias Stillblade, the knight who fell in the trial, knew well what he was sent to do, Bloodvalor says, and accepted his duty as an example to every aspiring Blood Knight. Nor is his service over: the initiate who slew him is to be the instrument of his resurrection. First, though, the initiate's education in the order's ways must go on, for it has only begun, and below the hall waits the truth of where the Blood Knights' mastery of the Light comes from.
sources: quests 9681, 9684, 9685 (descriptions and reward texts)
npc_text 12370 (Astalor gossip)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Blood_Knight (M'uru beneath the Hall of Blood, stolen by Kael's felblood elves)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/A_Study_in_Power (pre-2.4 and post-2.4 texts)
notes: Converted: the captive naaru moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9681); the vessel and Liadrin's search moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9684); Stillblade's resurrection moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9685). Opening is the 9681 description: Stillblade's coming resurrection, the betrayal and the lost power source. Earlier: verified Check: the 9681 description's betrayal and lost power source (patch 2.4 text) moved from the opening to part 1 (minState 12, QUEST_ACCEPT 9681, where the description tells it); the naaru secret (9681 reward text, era-free) is part 2; the drained keepers and Liadrin's search are part 3 (minState 12, QUEST_DONE 9684); the resurrection (part 4) no longer leans on part 3, so a pre-2.4 reading runs opening, secret, resurrection. Opening padded from the pre-2.4 9681 text on the wiki.

parts.body: The order is wounded. Prince Kael'thas has betrayed his people, the Blood Knights have lost the source of their power, and initiates must now learn new methods of wielding the Light. Even so, Bloodvalor sends them on to Astalor.
sources: quest 9681 description (patch 2.4 text: the betrayal of Kael'thas and the loss of the power source)

parts.body: In the chamber below, Astalor tells the secret at the heart of the order. Its Light was taken from a being of immense power, a naaru that Prince Kael'thas sent to Silvermoon as a gift. The creature begrudged the elves its gifts, so the magisters devised a way to claim them on their own terms.
sources: quest 9681 reward text

parts.body: It is that naaru the order has lost, but its keepers still hold faint vestiges of its energy, and with an enchanted vessel the initiate draws out what remains. Astalor promises that the knights will fight back, for Lady Liadrin already seeks a new source of power.
sources: quest 9684 description
npc_text 12370

parts.body: The Light the initiate drew was just enough. In an upper room of the city's inn, where initiates had carried his body, Sangrias Stillblade was brought back to life by the one who had killed him. The Light will never come naturally to the Blood Knights, Bloodvalor admits, but they will not be thwarted by the will of a single being, and the initiate, knowing now the truth about the order's power, is granted the means to raise the fallen in the field.
sources: quest 9685 description and reward text
quest 9684 reward text

title: The Master's Path
body: Blood Knights who rise far enough may be summoned by Lord Solanar Bloodwrath, Lady Liadrin's right hand, who offers to sponsor them for the order's inner circle of masters, the most dedicated, skilled and trusted of its knights, known to most only by their thalassian chargers. Candidates must prove their devotion to the order's tenets in tasks set from the easiest to the hardest. The first is humble: supplying cloth, metal, herbs, runes and gold so that Magister Astalor's men can keep the knights stocked with Light energy.
sources: quests 9721, 9722, 9723, 9725, 9735, 9736, 9737 (descriptions and reward texts)
creature_queststarter: 17717 starts 9721; 25223 starts 9722-9737
notes: Converted: the Scourge siege company beaten moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9725); the holy water and reagents moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9736); the chapel's flame quenched and the master's charger moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9737). Earlier: verified

parts.body: Next came loyalty, for the Blood Knights are bound to defend Quel'Thalas. A Scourge siege company of engineers and meat wagons was massing in the Eastern Plaguelands to strike at the Ghostlands, and the candidate broke it before it could move. One last task remained before the title of master.
sources: quest 9725 description and reward text

parts.body: The last task is a message to every other order of paladins, who despise the Blood Knights for unleashing the Light's true potential. The candidate stole holy water from the library of Tyr's Hand Abbey, its blessing tainted by the Scarlet Crusade's misguided zeal, and bought rare reagents from Silvermoon's shops, and Solanar prepared his mixture.
sources: quests 9735, 9736 descriptions and reward texts

parts.body: The mixture was carried to the Alonsus Chapel, where the Order of the Silver Hand was founded and whose eternal flame had kept it untouched by the destruction of Stratholme. With the flame quenched, the Light's protection was stripped away. The message delivered, the candidate took a place among the masters, with the right to summon a thalassian charger.
sources: quest 9737 description, completion and reward text

title: Envoy to the Horde
body: When the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir, who opened Quel'Thalas to the Scourge, falls at last in the Ghostlands, his head is carried to Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron in Sunfury Spire. The news is better than it seems. Some in the Horde had doubted the blood elves, asking what use a people could be who could not set their own lands in order, and now no one can question their power. Lor'themar sends a letter to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner in the Undercity, already a friend to his people, in the hope that she will send it on to Orgrimmar and that the elves may join the Horde as equals.
sources: quests 9328, 9811 (head of Dar'Khan to Lor'themar)
quests 9621, 9812 (Envoy to the Horde descriptions and Sylvanas's reward texts)
quest 9627 description and reward text (Thrall crushes the letter; link with Outland, not exactly the truth)
creature_queststarter: 16802 starts 9621 and 9812; 4949 Thrall starts 9627
notes: Converted: Sylvanas's welcome and her seal moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9621 for blood elves, 9812 for the other Horde races); Thrall's acceptance moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9626 or 9813, where he reads the letter; trimmed to what both reveal); the crushed letter, the Outland hope and the official joining moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9627, blood elves only). Opening keeps Dar'Khan's death, since both entry triggers come after it. Earlier: verified

parts.body: The Dark Lady heard the news gladly: the foul traitor had got what he deserved. She had fought hard for Silvermoon's place beside Undercity and Orgrimmar, and now, adding her own seal to Lor'themar's letter as a personal endorsement, she sent it on to Thrall, who as Warchief would have the final say.
sources: quests 9621, 9812 reward text
quests 9626, 9813 descriptions

parts.body: Thrall read the letter and found no more cause for doubt. The elves had seen a powerful Scourge leader destroyed at the doorstep of their home, and the Warchief admitted that the Horde needs them as much as they need the Horde. Quel'Thalas was welcomed among his allies.
sources: quests 9626, 9813 reward text
quest 9627 description

parts.body: For the blood elves the Warchief had a blunter answer: he crushed the letter in his fist and bade the elf welcome. Back in Silvermoon, Lor'themar reveals that Thrall also hopes the elves' link with Outland will help him reach his own people there, a belief the regent admits is not exactly the truth, though not a lie either. The sin'dorei are now officially part of the Horde.
sources: quest 9627 description and reward text
